Definition: hetchelling (or combing flax), i.e. (concretely) tow (by extension, linen cloth)
BiblicalUsage: Seriqah is tow, the combed flax, and Isaiah says the workers in fine flax shall be confounded when Egypt is judged.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the flax workers are the picture of an economy judged: the hands that spin the fine cloth find nothing left to spin.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
